articles.headline: Commanders rule RG Cosmi, TE Okonkwo, LB Luvu out Sunday
articles.description: Right guard Sam Cosmi (concussion), tight end Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) and linebacker Frankie Luvu (groin) won't play Sunday vs. the Seahawks.
articles.body:
ASHBURN, Va. -- The Washington Commanders ruled out three starters for Sunday's game against the visiting Seattle Seahawks, further depleting their roster.

Right guard Sam Cosmi (concussion), tight end Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) and linebacker Frankie Luvu (groin) won't play, according to the game status report released Friday.

Washington (0-2) already was without quarterback Jayden Daniels (dislocated elbow) and safety Nick Cross (internal injury).

 

Luvu and Okonkwo missed the 37-20 loss at Dallas in Week 2. The other three players were hurt vs. the Cowboys; Cross needed to stay overnight in a Dallas hospital.

Leo Chenal replaced Luvu in the starting lineup next to rookie Sonny Styles. Luvu was Washington's defensive playcaller, but Styles handled that in Week 2.

Cross will be difficult to replace because he lines up in a variety of positions, from linebacker in some packages to a box safety and deep safety. Quan Martin will replace him in the starting lineup; coaches like his versatility as well.

Okonkwo was signed in the offseason to provide explosive plays downfield. Without him, the team will use a rotation of John Bates, Ben Sinnott and Colson Yankoff. But the Commanders also like to use three-receiver sets. They've used that look 67.9% of the time through two games.

Cosmi suffered the concussion in the fourth quarter vs. Dallas. Washington could replace him by moving Nick Allegretti from center to guard, where he has started the bulk of his career, and inserting veteran Lucas Patrick at center. The Commanders could start veteran Andrew Wylie at guard as well.

Washington has lost 12 of its past 14 games dating to last season. The Commanders lost their opener at Philadelphia 24-22. They still have four players on injured reserve, including projected starting cornerback Trey Amos (ankle). The others are linebacker Jordan Magee (hamstring), defensive end Deatrich Wise Jr. (quad) and running back Jeremy McNichols (quad).

The good news for Washington is that Daniels is expected to return soon from his dislocated left elbow, though it's uncertain how many games he will miss.

articles.headline: Rio Ferdinand leads reaction to Man City's 115 breaches case: 'Another Premier League medal'
articles.description: The football world has been reacting to reports that Manchester City are expected to be found guilty of most charges in their legal battle with the Premier League.
articles.body:
The football world has been reacting to reports that a decision on Manchester City's longstanding legal battle with the Premier League over an alleged 115 breaches of financial regulations may be right around the corner. 

City are expected to be found guilty on the vast majority of charges of financial breaches in their legal case with the Premier League, a source has confirmed to ESPN.

In a statement, City didn't deny the verdicts and said that the process "remains ongoing."

When contacted by ESPN on Friday, the Premier League said they wouldn't comment on a "private and confidential process."

Friday's reports have given fresh impetus to speculation that City could be in line for a hefty punishment, with some hoping the major honours they won during the period covered by the investigation (2009-2018) could be redistributed to their beaten foes. 

David de Gea, who was part of the Manchester United team that finished as runners-up when City racked up 100 points in 2017-18, wrote in a post on X: "So... Let's talk. How many Premier League titles have I won then?"

His former United teammate Rio Ferdinand posted: "Another premier league medal to be added to the cabinet."

Rodri, who left City for Barcelona this summer, said he believes "everything was deserved." Rodri joined City from Atletico Madrid in 2019, one year after the end of the period in which the charges relate.

"When you live daily at that club, all the people that worked hard all these years to have the success we had, Pep, the owners, all the guys who worked on it, they can't take that from us. It's something that isn't paid for with money, it's effort, partnership, standing shoulder to shoulder," he told a news conference ahead of Spain's Nations League match against England.

"We had a lot of success, here at Wembley, and I can tell you that everything was deserved."

José Mourinho has said in 2024 that he was still hopeful he could become a Premier League champion with United if City are found guilty.

"We finished second in the Premier League," Mourinho said at a news conference during his time at Fenerbahce. "I think we still have a chance to win that league because maybe they punish Man City with points and maybe we win that league and they have to pay me the bonus and give me the medal."

Jürgen Klopp, whose Liverpool team regularly went toe-to-toe with Guardiola's City in more recent years, said in 2025 that he would throw a party on the island of Mallorca should the Premier League strip City of their titles.

Information from ESPN's Alex Kirkland contributed to this story.

articles.headline: Rodri 'believes in innocence' of Man City, says success 'deserved'
articles.description: Former Manchester City midfielder Rodri has said he "believes in the innocence of the club" after reports that City were set to be found guilty on most of the charges brought by the Premier League over alleged breaches of financial rules.
articles.body:
Former Manchester City midfielder Rodri said he "believes in the innocence of the club" after reports that City were set to be found guilty on most of the charges brought by the Premier League over alleged breaches of financial rules.

A source confirmed to ESPN that City were expected to be found guilty on the vast majority of the 115 charges of financial breaches in their legal case with the Premier League.

- Man City vs. Premier League: 115 financial charges explained

- Rio Ferdinand leads reaction to Man City's 115 breaches case

Rodri -- who will captain world champions Spain at Wembley on Saturday as they face England in the UEFA Nations League -- spent seven years at City before joining Barcelona this summer.

City did not deny the reports, while the league refused to comment, stating that the process was confidential.

"We experienced an identical process in 2020, if I remember rightly," Rodri said in a news conference at Wembley on Friday, referring to UEFA's investigation into City, which saw them initially banned from European competitions before the verdict was overturned on appeal.

"From the club, they always told us to be calm, that we'd be acquitted, that we hadn't done anything, and the club was found not guilty ... Let's hope justice can be done.

"But I believe in the innocence of the club. I know the club well. We were told at the time to be calm, and that everything had been done properly."

The Premier League charges relate to a period before Rodri joined City in 2019.

The 2024 Ballon d'Or winner won four Premier League titles with City between 2020 and 2024, as well as the 2023 Champions League.

"For us the players, it's a different thing than for you guys [the media]," Rodri said, when asked again about the charges. "I understand all kinds of opinions. It's something that's big now, but we always try to think positive.

"When you live daily at that club, with all the people that worked hard all these years to have the success we had, with Pep [Guardiola], the owners, everyone who worked on that ... They can't take that from us.

"It's something that isn't paid for with money, it's effort, partnership, standing shoulder to shoulder. We had a lot of success, here at Wembley, and I can tell you that everything was deserved."

Rodri was asked how he would feel if the guilty charges were to be confirmed, having been assured by City bosses of the club's innocence.

"They [the club] always told us the confidence they had in their innocence, and when you look in someone's eyes and they tell you that ..." Rodri said. "We were always calm, we never saw the team [being] nervous with these kinds of things.

"Everyone has to follow the rules, I support that, but it's part of football today. They always expressed confidence that they never did anything wrong, and we believed in that. I've been there, I know how they work, so that's what I can tell you."

articles.headline: Source: Man City set to be found guilty on majority of Premier League charges
articles.description: Manchester City are expected to be found guilty on the vast majority of charges of financial breaches in their legal case with the Premier League, a source confirmed to ESPN.
articles.body:
Manchester City are expected to be found guilty on the vast majority of charges of financial breaches in their legal case with the Premier League, a source confirmed to ESPN.

In a statement, City didn't deny the guilty verdicts and said that the process "remains ongoing."

When contacted by ESPN on Friday, the Premier League said it wouldn't comment on a "private and confidential process."

The Athletic first reported Friday that City had been found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges by an independent panel.

One source has told ESPN that City sought an injunction Friday to block initial reporting of the verdict. City strongly denied that is the case when approached by ESPN.

It is expected that City -- which could face anything from a fine to a points deduction or even expulsion from the Premier League by way of punishment -- will appeal any guilty verdict.

A statement issued by City on Friday read: "The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality. As such Manchester City FC's position remains consistent with the club's statement of February 2023.

"The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence."

The Premier League announced the charges against City in February 2023 following a four-year investigation.

The case was heard at an independent hearing at the International Dispute Resolution Centre in London, beginning in September 2024. It came to an end in December 2024 after 12 weeks of deliberations.

The alleged breaches of financial rules were said to have occurred over a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018.

The Premier League's claim was centered around its belief that City did not provide "accurate financial information that gives a true and fair view of the club's financial position."

City have maintained their innocence throughout the process.

In February 2020, City were found guilty of breaking UEFA's financial fair play rules and given a two-year ban from European competition and €30m fine.

The suspension was lifted by the Court of Arbitration for Sport five months later with the fine reduced to €10m.

articles.headline: Grizzlies waive veteran point guard D'Angelo Russell
articles.description: The Memphis Grizzlies waived veteran D'Angelo Russell and signed undrafted guard Brendan Hausen.
articles.body:
The Memphis Grizzlies have waived veteran point guard D'Angelo Russell, making him a free agent one month before the start of the season.

Russell, 30, began last season with the Dallas Mavericks but has since been traded twice, first to Washington as part of the Anthony Davis trade in February and then to Memphis as part of a six-team deal over the summer. He never ended up playing a game for the Wizards or Grizzlies.

Russell averaged 10.2 points and 4.0 assists in 26 games for Dallas last year. His last strong year came in 2023-24 for the Los Angeles Lakers, when he averaged 18 points and five assists, and he's been traded several times since.

In a corresponding roster move Friday, the Grizzlies signed undrafted guard Brendan Hausen, who played four seasons at Kansas State and Iowa.

articles.headline: Vikings' Aaron Jones Sr. (knee) cleared to play vs. Buccaneers
articles.description: Vikings RB Aaron Jones Sr. has been cleared to start Sunday against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers after leaving Week 2's win over the Bears in a knee brace.
articles.body:
EAGAN, Minn. -- Minnesota Vikings running back Aaron Jones Sr. was a full participant in practice Friday and has been cleared to start Sunday's game at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Jones, 31, took 23 carries in a Week 2 victory over the Chicago Bears and finished the game wearing a knee brace. He did not practice Wednesday, but he said Friday that he never doubted he would be ready to play.

"I finished the game last week," Jones said, "so in my head I was good to go for this week."

It remains to be seen whether Jones will take on the same load he did in Chicago. The Vikings likely will throw more frequently against the Buccaneers with starter Kyler Murray back in the starting lineup. To this point, the Vikings rank No. 2 in the NFL in designed run rate (50%) after playing most of their two games with backup Carson Wentz in the game.

Jones likely will be backed up by veteran DeeJay Dallas and rookie Demond Claiborne. Veteran Jordan Mason opened the season as Jones' backup but will be on injured reserve for at least two more weeks because of a fractured thumb.

"I don't know what kind of load I'm getting," Jones said, "but when my number's called, I'll be ready. I like those kind of games. ... And if it turns into that, I'm ready."

articles.headline: Chiefs CB Mansoor Delane set to play after missing win over Colts
articles.description: Chiefs coach Andy Reid says rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane, who does not have a designation on the injury report, has a "good chance" of playing against the Dolphins.
articles.body:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. -- Chiefs rookie cornerback Mansoor Delane, who is recovering from a right shoulder injury, is expected to start in Sunday's road game against the Miami Dolphins.

Coach Andy Reid said Friday that Delane has a "good chance" of playing after being a full participant in each of the Chiefs' three practices this week. Delane also does not have a designation on the injury report.

Delane, the Chiefs' top draft pick, was in uniform last week for the team's overtime win against the Indianapolis Colts but was held out for precautionary reasons.

In the Chiefs' season-opening win over the Denver Broncos, Delane aggravated his right shoulder injury after he intercepted quarterback Bo Nix. Delane's 5-yard return ended when he stumbled and fell to the turf, landing on his right shoulder, with the injury forcing him to miss the rest of the game.

"It wasn't coming around as fast as we wanted," Reid said Monday of Delane's shoulder. "He was right on the border there. He wanted to suit up, and if needed, he could have gone in, but we're trying to keep him out of having to play a full game."

In June, Delane missed the Chiefs' mandatory minicamp because he sustained a hairline fracture in his scapula, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. Kansas City traded with the Cleveland Browns, moving up from the ninth pick to No. 6, to draft Delane.

The Chiefs on Friday also listed left tackle Josh Simmons (lower back) as out and safety Chamarri Conner (right knee) as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Dolphins.

articles.headline: Texans WR Nico Collins (hamstring) to miss second straight game
articles.description: The Texans will be without Pro Bowl wideout Nico Collins for the second straight week when they travel to face the Colts.
articles.body:
HOUSTON -- The Texans will be without Pro Bowl wideout Nico Collins for the second straight week when they travel to face the Colts.

Collins did not practice this week and was ruled out Friday.

The injury isn't nearly as severe as his hamstring injury from 2024, when he landed on injured reserve after Week 5 and missed five games. Collins' next chance to play will be when Houston host the Dallas Cowboys in Week 4.

The Texans have struggled at times to score without their No. 1 wideout, including during last week's 20-6 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals when quarterback C.J. Stroud threw for 353 yards but Houston never reached the end zone. Houston has averaged 16 points in the past three games that Collins has missed because of injury.

The key in the struggles is receivers not stepping up in Collins' absence. In those three games, no receiver has eclipsed 70 receiving yards and only three have gone over 55.

Tight end Dalton Schultz produced in a big way against the Bengals, totaling 140 yards on 12 receptions. But no other receiver eclipsed 37 yards.

Houston will rely on wideouts Xavier Hutchinson, Jaylin Noel, Jared Wayne and Kayshon Boutte to make life easier whenever Stroud tries to throw outside the numbers. The Texans also need their running game to produce. Last week, running backs Woody Marks and David Montgomery totaled 18 yards on 14 carries.
